title.rendered: Learning Watercolors with Alejandro Piñeiro Bello

content.rendered:
Participants in the Learning Watercolors workshop will create watercolor paintings on paper guided by artist Alejandro Piñeiro Bello. Families will explore the fluidity and freshness of the medium, drawing inspiration from works on view at the museum, the surrounding gardens, nature, sunlight, landscape, and architecture, as well as ideas that emerge through the process of painting.

The program begins at 11 am with an artist meet-and-greet and refreshments. The workshop runs from 11:30 am to 1 pm, followed by lunch in the ICA Miami Sculpture Garden.

title.rendered: Friedrich Kunath in conversation with Klaus Biesenbach, Director of the Neue Nationalgalerie and Berlin Modern

content.rendered:
Program Presented by DMINTI, Nassima Foundation, and ICA Miami.

ICA Miami, DMINTI, and the Nassima Foundation are pleased to present Klaus Biesenbach in conversation with Friedrich Kunath at ICA Miami’s expansion space. The event will take place on December 1 at 11 AM ET during Art Basel Miami Beach 2026.

The conversation centers on Friedrich Kunath’s longstanding engagement with German Romanticism and the influence of Caspar David Friedrich on his work. The dialogue will explore how themes such as landscape, melancholy, and the sublime are reflected and interpreted in Kunath’s contemporary practice, alongside the influence of American popular culture.

excerpt.rendered: Join Friedrich Kunath and Klaus Biesenbach for a panel conversation at ICA Miami on Dec 1, 2026 at 11 am, celebrating Kunath’s first U.S. solo show.

title.rendered: A+RC Virtual Lecture by Domietta Torlasco: Quantum Cinema: For a New Politics of Location

content.rendered:
ICA Miami welcomes Domietta Torlasco, Professor of Comparative Literature at Northwestern University, for a virtual lecture. This lecture is free and open to the public with advance RSVP and is presented in conjunction with A +RC Fall 2026 semester: New Approaches to Cinema.

Film and photography have traditionally been understood as media of indexicality, capable of providing a veritable trace of what is in front of the camera. The camera, especially in its mechanical version, has long been hailed as the guarantor of evidence. Even today, audiovisual recordings hold the power to bear witness to momentous but otherwise fugitive events. On the other hand, new technologies—from Augmented Reality (AR) to Artificial Intelligence (AI)—seem to erode or even undo this capacity to record what really happened in a specific place at a specific point in time. This lecture is an invitation to step back and ask what we mean by location—to move beyond the constraints of classical physics and explore cinema’s historical capacity to bear witness to a more complex reality. What claims of truth and justice can be made in this other location opened up by technology? How can we reconceive of our responsibility as both spectators and makers of images?

title.rendered: A+RC Virtual Lecture by Homay King: Better Living in Eichlerville: California Modernism’s Influence on Apple

content.rendered:
ICA Miami welcomes Homay King, Professor of Art History and Digital Media at Bryn Mawr College, to the Art + Research Center for a virtual lecture. This lecture is free and open to the public with advance RSVP and is presented in conjunction with A +RC Fall 2026 semester: New Approaches to Cinema.

This talk studies a set of Californian suburban tract housing developments built by Joseph Eichler during the 1950s-1970s.

Working with architects who had studied California Modernism with Richard Neutra and his circle, Eichler aimed to bring Bauhaus-inspired designs for modern living to middle-class Californians, concentrated in Silicon Valley along the San Francisco peninsula. His mass-produced, post-and-beam construction homes made with natural materials would soon become a recognizable hallmark of the California suburbs, featured in photography, films, and music videos. Eichler homes—with their flat, opaque, nearly windowless front facades and transparent glass backs—reversed the dominant model of suburban domestic architecture, which had been characterized by front-facing “picture windows.”

Eichler’s tract housing shaped the design of personal computers that were being produced in the same place and time: Steve Jobs grew up in an Eichler look-alike and cited its influence on his aesthetic. Digital technology design, King argues, drew upon California Modernist principles of seamless minimalism, privacy and private property, and “indoor-outdoor living.”

The talk also addresses Eichler’s public advocacy for open-access housing, which led to surprisingly diverse demographics in these neighborhoods at a time when many suburbs practiced legally enforced segregation. The presentation is derived from King’s book manuscript in progress, Go West: A Mythology of California’s Silicon Valley.

title.rendered: A+RC Virtual Lecture by Zabet Patterson: Inhuman Worlds: Pierre Huyghe’s Liminal

content.rendered:
ICA Miami welcomes Zabet Patterson, Professor of Art History at Stony Brook University, to the Art + Research Center for a virtual lecture. This lecture is free and open to the public with advance RSVP and is presented in conjunction with A +RC Fall 2026 semester: New Approaches to Cinema.

Pierre Huyghe’s 2024 exhibition Liminal, staged in the cavernous spaces of the Punta della Dogana in Venice, is a dense tangle of apparatuses, operators, subjects, and intelligences: bodies whose movements are driven in real time by environmental sensors, neural-net reconstructions of brain images of an imagined character, and machines performing uncanny rituals over a skeleton in the Atacama desert.

This lecture works through three central works – Liminal, UUmwelt-Annlee, and Camata – to argue that machine learning and AI architecture produce both a dispositif, an assemblage of apparatuses, and an emergent umwelt, in N. Katherine Hayles’s translation of von Uexküll’s term as “world-horizon.” Huyghe foregrounds the imagistic and representational only to insist on the radical opacity of these systems: shells without interiority, and surfaces whose data we provide but whose sensorial affordances and analytic depths we cannot access.

What follows when networked computational systems have become world-generating environments – when the image-world begins to observe us before we observe it, and to compose in a cinematic language we made but no longer control?

title.rendered: Family Sundays at ICA Miami: Special Event with Katy Hessel

content.rendered: Join art historian and bestselling author Katy Hessel for a special family book talk celebrating the release of The Story of Art Without Men: An Illustrated Guide to Amazing Women Artists, introducing young readers to the groundbreaking women artists too often left out of history. Through interactive discussion, drawing, and visual storytelling, Hessel invites families to participate in expanding the story of art history and discover how art can always be relevant to them. Ages 7+.

title.rendered: Family Sundays at ICA Miami: Music & Movement with Paloma Dueñas

content.rendered: Inspired by Manoucher Yektai’s Curtain and Still Life and the untitled works in the first-floor gallery, families will explore vibrant color and dynamic composition through expressive movement and music. Together, we’ll experiment with different rhythms, musical dynamics, instruments, and sensory scarves to translate the energy of the artworks into playful movement and sound.

excerpt.rendered: Bring art to life with Paloma Dueñas. Families will translate Manoucher Yektai’s dynamic paintings into playful sound, rhythm, and expressive scarf movement.

title.rendered: Family Sundays at ICA Miami: Storytelling with Ms. Krystal

content.rendered: Based on Manoucher Yektai’s “The Stranger and the Tree,” join Ms. Krystal for a special bilingual musical storytime as we dig into new beginnings and the magic of finding our place. Yektai writes that it is perhaps the solitary tree “who has not considered where to put roots / On a crackless rock out of place . . . without soil” who “will live, will thrive, will give fruit.” Let’s sing, read, and explore new imagined lands together!

excerpt.rendered: Sing, read, and explore at ICA Miami’s Family Sundays. Ms. Krystal leads a bilingual musical storytelling session inspired by Manoucher Yektai’s poetry and art.

title.rendered: Harmony Korine in Conversation with Craig Robins and Alex Gartenfeld

content.rendered:
Join legendary filmmaker and artist Harmony Korine in conversation with entrepreneur and philanthropist Craig Robins and Alex Gartenfeld, Irma and Norman Braman Artistic Director at ICA Miami. Taking place in conjunction with Harmony Korine: Perfect Nonsense, the first U.S. museum survey of Korine’s multifaceted practice. The conversation will consider the artist’s expansive approach to image-making and his movement across cinema, painting, photography, collage, drawing, and experimental media.

Since entering the public consciousness at nineteen as the screenwriter of the generation-defining film Kids (1995), Korine has continually expanded the language of cinema while challenging distinctions between contemporary art, popular culture, and the moving image. The conversation will explore his ongoing experiments with new technologies and forms, as well as the influence of Miami, his home since 2015, on his recent work through the experimental media company EDGLRD.

Harmony Korine: Perfect Nonsense is on view at ICA Miami through October 18, 2026.

excerpt.rendered: Join Harmony Korine, Craig Robins and Alex Gartenfeld at ICA Miami on Oct 1, 2026. Discover Korine’s multifaceted career, from Kids to EDGLRD, alongside the Perfect Nonsense survey.

title.rendered: Family Fest 2026: We Are Miami

content.rendered:
This year’s Family Fest celebrates “We Are Miami,” bringing families together for a day inspired by the people, places, and creative energy that define our city. Through art, music, performance, and hands-on experiences, families will discover the stories and cultural traditions of Miami’s distinctive communities – from Little Haiti and Little Havana to Miami Beach, Wynwood, and the Design District.

Throughout the day, ICA Miami comes alive with opportunities to make, explore, move, and create together, celebrating Miami as a city shaped by many histories, perspectives, and forms of creative expression.

What to expect:

  • Neighborhood Art Expeditions: Explore the neighborhoods of Miami through murals created by local artists inspired by the layered histories, architecture, art, and design of Little Haiti, Little Havana, Miami Beach, Wynwood, and Miami Design District.
  • Hands-On Art Making: Create something of your own at artist-led activity stations designed for kids and grown-ups to experience together.
  • Live Performances: Experience a lively, interactive 40-minute performance by Miami’s own Fantasy Theatre, bringing music, movement, and storytelling into the museum.

Your ticket purchase directly supports ICA Miami’s free weekend programming for youth, helping make meaningful arts experiences accessible to young people throughout our community.

Ticket Pricing

  • Adults: $50
  • Kids: $15
  • Children under 3: Free

Location

ICA Miami Expansion Space
23 NE 41st St, Miami, FL 33137

excerpt.rendered: Explore the art, rhythms, and culture of Miami’s iconic neighborhoods. Join us for a family festival celebrating community, creativity, and local pride.
